insights.concise_text: On the 20Newsgroups dataset, Oracle-99 needs more annotations with larger batch percents, consistent with decreased learning efficiency with larger batch sizes.

triple.subject: Oracle-99 on 20Newsgroups
triple.object: more annotations with larger batch percents due to decreased learning efficiency

insights.concise_text: For larger batch percents, BV2009 stops later than the optimal Oracle Method point, while Oracle-99 is the Oracle Method with the percentage set to 99.

triple.subject: BV2009
triple.object: the optimal Oracle Method point defined by Oracle-99

insights.concise_text: Using a window size of one lets BV2009 stop with fewer annotations than a window size of three without losing much F-Measure, supporting smaller window sizes as mitigation.

triple.subject: BV2009 with window size of one
triple.object: BV2009 with window size of three by reducing annotations without much F-Measure loss

insights.concise_text: Larger batch percents generate fewer models, giving BV2009 fewer stopping points and causing somewhat sub-optimal stopping with very large batch percents.

triple.subject: larger batch percents
triple.object: BV2009 to stop somewhat sub-optimally through fewer models and fewer stopping points

insights.concise_text: Because BV2009 needs models before checking the average kappa threshold, low early kappa agreement scores combined with fewer stopping points explain sub-optimal stopping at very large batch percents.

triple.subject: BV2009's model requirement and low early kappa agreement scores
triple.object: stopping quality at very large batch percents

insights.concise_text: The paper evaluates batch sizes of 1%, 5%, and 10% of the training data on 20Newsgroups using a Support Vector Machine and closest-to-hyperplane sampling.

triple.subject: the batch-size evaluation on 20Newsgroups
triple.object: a Support Vector Machine and closest-to-hyperplane sampling

insights.concise_text: Stopping methods enable active learning's annotation-cost benefits in practice, but larger batch sizes degrade stopping method performance beyond decreased learning efficiency.

triple.subject: larger batch sizes
triple.object: the practical annotation-cost benefits enabled by stopping methods

insights.concise_text: The tension between smaller batch sizes for learning efficiency and larger batch sizes for development speed motivates analyzing stopping method parameters such as window size.

triple.subject: the batch-size tension
triple.object: analysis of stopping method parameters such as window size

insights.concise_text: Oracle-99 contextualizes practical stopping results because the Oracle Method cannot be used in practice and BV2009 is compared against the optimal Oracle Method point.

triple.subject: Oracle-99
triple.object: contextualization of practical stopping results including BV2009

insights.concise_text: The degradation in stopping method performance with larger batch sizes is larger than degradation explained by learning efficiency, and smaller window sizes help mitigate it.
